alt: A ladder of five sizes running from the 0.1 mm limit of unaided vision down to the 2 nm width of the DNA double helix, with a modelled crypt opening, one crypt cell, and the light-microscope limit in between.
longDescription: Five rungs, largest at the top. Rung one: the finest detail the unaided eye separates, about 0.1 millimetres, which is 100 micrometres. Rung two: a modelled colonic crypt opening. In a simplified circular model, 22 cells of about 10 micrometres around the perimeter imply an opening about 70 micrometres across, which is finer than the eye threshold and so is not resolved by it. Rung three: one colonic epithelial cell, about 10 to 20 micrometres across, five to ten times finer than the eye threshold, and that is the gap a lens had to close. Rung four: the finest detail a conventional light microscope separates, about 0.25 micrometres, which is 250 nanometres. Rung five: the DNA double helix, about 2 nanometres across, roughly a hundred times finer than the light-microscope limit, so no conventional light microscope shows it. Crypt depth is not used to decide what a surface view resolves.
